findings.obs_text: In Psa 145:5 wondrous (H6381) stands two words before meditate and describes what is meditated on: the works of God are the object, set first in the verse.
findings.grounds: on your wondrous works, I will meditate

findings.obs_text: In Jos 1:8 careful (H8104J) stands four words after meditate, in the purpose it serves: the meditating day and night is so that the person keeps to doing what is written.
findings.grounds: so that you may be careful to do

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:99 more understanding (H7919A) opens the verse and the meditation closes it as its ground: the testimonies being the speaker's meditation is given as why he understands more than his teachers.
findings.grounds: for your testimonies are my meditation

findings.obs_text: In Psa 1:2 delight (H2656) opens the verse and the meditating follows in the next clause, both on the law of the Lord: the delight and the meditation have one object.
findings.grounds: his delight is in the law of the Lord

findings.obs_text: In Psa 104:34 pleasing (H6149) stands directly after meditation and says what the speaker asks of it: that it please the Lord.
findings.grounds: May my meditation be pleasing to him

older.finding: the scoffer painted by what he will not receive: rebuke (Pro 13:1, 15:12)
older.reason: it states how the scoffer refuses rebuke; its words are of many collections, scoff the one it is about

findings.obs_text: In Jos 1:8 depart (H4185) stands three words before meditate, in the clause it is set against: the book is not to leave the mouth, and instead it is meditated on.
findings.grounds: shall not depart from your mouth

findings.obs_text: In Psa 38:12 ruin (H1942) stands directly before meditate, the speaking of ruin joined to the devising of treachery by those who seek harm.
findings.grounds: speak of ruin and meditate treachery

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:78 wronged (H5791) stands three words before meditate, in the clause about the insolent; the speaker's meditating is set against their wronging.
findings.grounds: they have wronged me with falsehood

findings.obs_text: In Pro 15:28 wicked (H7563) stands three words after ponders, on the other side of the contrast: the righteous heart ponders, the mouth of the wicked pours out.
findings.grounds: the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things

older.finding: wicked as the wickedness or ungodliness of a person, a state or practice of the heart
older.reason: it states a face of the wicked words; the evildoer collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 77:3 faints (H5848C) stands two words after meditate, in the same clause: when the speaker meditates, his spirit faints.
findings.grounds: when I meditate, my spirit faints

findings.obs_text: In Job 15:4 fear (H3374) stands two words before meditation, in the first of two parallel charges: the fear of God is set aside, and meditation before God is held back.
findings.grounds: doing away with the fear of God

findings.obs_text: In Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5 remember (H2142) stands before meditate, one to three words ahead, in parallel clauses: remembering comes first and meditating follows.
findings.grounds: I remember the days of old; I meditate

older.finding: remembering weighs on the soul; memory works either way (Lam 3:17, 3:20; Psa 42:4)
older.reason: it states how remembering works on the soul; the forget collection owns the remembering words

older.finding: under the enemy the spirit faints and the heart is appalled, then remembering, thirst and the plea follow (Psa 143:3-7)
older.reason: it states how the spirit faints under pursuit and what follows; the faint collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 104:34 rejoice (H8055) stands three words after meditation, in the clause that follows it: the speaker rejoices in the Lord.
findings.grounds: for I rejoice in the Lord

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:15, Psa 119:27 and Psa 119:78 precepts (H6490) stands beside meditate as what is meditated on, or as the way the speaker asks to understand before he meditates.
findings.grounds: I will meditate on your precepts

findings.obs_text: In Psa 19:14, Psa 49:3, Psa 77:6, Pro 15:28 and Luk 2:19 heart (H3820A, H3824, G2588) stands beside the meditation or the pondering, one to three words off, as where it takes place: the meditation of the heart, meditating in the heart, the heart that ponders.

older.finding: haste or pause of the heart: haste (Job 20:2, Pro 21:5), pause (Pro 15:28, Psa 4:4, Dan 7:28)
older.reason: it states how the heart hastens or pauses; the heart collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 77:12, Psa 143:5 and Psa 145:5 work and works (H6467, H4639G, H1697K) stand beside meditate as what is meditated on: the deeds of God.
In Psa 77:3 moan (H1993) stands one word before meditate, in the parallel clause: remembering God brings moaning, meditating brings the spirit's fainting.
findings.grounds: When I remember God, I moan
